fills.researcher_notes: Sheet Operator blank. The Ukrainian section runs Khust→Tekovo metering station in Zakarpattia Oblast; Owner already reads GTSOU [100.%]. The Romanian side beyond the border is Transgaz's, which is why the operator cell should be read as the UKRAINIAN section's operator on a cross-border row. Independence: counted as two independent origins — ENTSOG's own membership register and Ukrtransgaz/TSOUA's own archived key-facts page. uk.wikipedia is carried as a reading aid for the Ukrainian-language corporate history and is NOT counted toward independence (tertiary encyclopaedia). Same ref triple used across this brief's rows, per the Leg-3 instruction to settle the operator question once per company.

Ref-only, no value change: EEGA's Table 1 gives 2 bcm/yr for the Tekovo crossing, matching the sheet's 2.00 bcm/y exactly. This is the second of the scope's two capacity refs and the cleaner one — source and sheet agree.

validity.recommendation: No change. Record in ResearcherNotes that 20.60 km is the UKRAINIAN section to the border metering station while the drawn 52.8 km is the full cross-border Khust→Satu Mare corridor — the 2.57 ratio is a units-of-account difference, not an error in either.
validity.researcher_notes: The geojson correctly draws the full Khust→Satu Mare corridor (52.8 km measured). EEGA names the crossing's metering station as TEKOVO, which geocodes to (23.0956, 48.1224), about 21.5 km from Khust — within a kilometre of the sheet's 20.60 km. So both numbers are right and they count different things: GEM's length is the Ukrainian section, the route is the whole line. Flagged rather than silently closed because the row's country columns (Ukraine→Romania) invite the whole-corridor reading, so the distinction belongs in the cell notes.
